title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Equation numbering: the page's displayed map is (76), not (75); (75) ended the previous page.

Minor ambiguity: the composites u·a^{-1}·τ'^{ν} mix automorphisms and group elements. Grothendieck himself notes in the margin that i_ρ(a), i_σ(b) should be written. The claim α ∈ Ĝ ('donc α, β ∈ 𝔖') is under-justified on the page: it needs u·i_ρ(a)^{-1} to be in τ'^{ν'}·Inn, which is precisely the fibre-product condition.
Injectivity relies on u being determined by its values on ρ and σ, i.e. on ρ and σ topologically generating Ĝ^+. This is implicit (true for Z/2 * Z/3) but not stated.

ideas.what: Parametrising a group of automorphisms of a profinite group preserving conjugacy classes of torsion generators (up to inversion) by solutions (α, β, μ) of a commutator ('loop') equation [α,ρ] = [β,σ]·ε_1^{μ-1}.
ideas.modern_name: GT-type description of Aut/Out of profinite PSL2(Z)-like groups; Drinfeld–Ihara style parametrisation (λ, f) of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s); for profinite PSL2(Z)/modular-group variants, Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished notes; the Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the GT program without these computations.

ideas.what: Fibre product S_0Γ of an automorphism group with normalisers N*_ρ, N*_σ, mapped bijectively onto the solution set, with free action of centraliser products giving the quotient Σ.
ideas.modern_name: Torsor and normaliser bookkeeping for lifting outer automorphisms to automorphisms

missed.claim: This is a detailed, independent (and likely pre-Drinfeld) treatment of the étale/automorphism part of a GT-like group attached to a free product of two finite cyclic groups. It identifies the automorphism data (u, a, b) with solutions of a commutator equation with a cyclotomic twist ε_1^{μ-1}. The computation itself is a routine verification, but it documents Grothendieck's own route to GT-type objects via a 'loop equation'.
missed.quote: la condition [α,ρ]=[β,σ]ε_1^{μ-1} ne fait qu'exprimer la condition que u(ε_0)=ε_0^μ qui intervient dans la définition de Z_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for the genesis of GT and its variants for the profinite modular group. It is mathematically close to known results (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki on automorphisms of profinite free products).

deep.surprise_reason: A careful routine verification step (injectivity of a canonical map) inside a known unpublished GT-type programme. Historically interesting, but no new result visible on this page.
